Engineering Overload and Platform Migration Delay

coaching.summary: The graph covers the main options and key risks well, but several high-stakes causal links are missing or underweighted. The two-quarter deadline combined with four already-committed engineers makes capacity the single most constraining factor, and that pressure deserves sharper representation.

strengthen_items.label: Connect platform migration demand directly to engineering capacity
strengthen_items.detail: Platform Migration Competing Demand currently only flows to Engineering Overload and Platform Migration Delay, but it should also reduce Engineering Capacity Allocated to Billing, making the capacity constraint explicit rather than implied.

strengthen_items.label: Quantify engineering capacity available per option
strengthen_items.detail: Assign concrete engineer-quarter estimates to each option's Engineering Capacity Allocated to Billing value so the two-quarter constraint becomes a hard filter rather than a soft concern.

strengthen_items.label: Add an integration-effort factor for the vendor path
strengthen_items.detail: Vendor solutions still require non-trivial integration work against your existing stack; without a factor capturing this, Buy Vendor Solution (Metronome or Orb) looks cheaper in engineering time than it likely is.

strengthen_items.label: Clarify what Delay Billing Migration (Status Quo) actually means for the goal
strengthen_items.detail: Delay Billing Migration (Status Quo) feeds all indicator factors simultaneously, which is structurally incoherent; clarify whether it represents 'do nothing' (billing stays broken) or a phased delay, and wire it only to the outcomes that apply.

elements_considered_but_excluded: customer-trust recovery cost node — the brief mentions it but Billing Errors Damaging Customer Trust already proxies it; adding a separate node would duplicate without new causal information given current graph scope
data-migration complexity node — relevant for stripe middleware but not enough graph evidence to anchor it

bias_signals.detail: The graph treats Time to Live (Quarters) as a factor each option sets independently, implying delivery timing is controllable; in practice, billing complexity and integration surprises make the two-quarter window highly uncertain for Build In-House Metering and Invoicing and Extend Stripe with Custom Middleware.

Delay Billing Migration (Status Quo) is modeled as a live option with full factor connections rather than as a dominated baseline, which may give it unwarranted analytical weight and obscure that delay itself carries the risk of ongoing billing breakage.

Vendor Lock-In and Pricing Dependency receives two incoming edges while Engineering Overload and Platform Migration Delay receives only two despite the brief explicitly flagging four already-committed engineers; the graph may be over-indexing on vendor risk relative to the more immediate capacity risk.
